newsitem.title: ITALY: Stolen Venice church statues found in rubbish bin.
newsitem.headline: Stolen Venice church statues found in rubbish bin.

text.p: A small bronze statue of a lion, which was stolen from St Mark's Basilica in Venice this week, was found by police in a rubbish bin on Saturday after an anonymous tip-off.
Two other bronze statues, part of an original set of four which were recently seized from another Venice church, were also recovered.
Police were directed to the street bin in the centre of Padua, a northern city close to Venice, by the unknown telephone caller early on Saturday.

The 17th century lion and the two 18th century pieces were discovered inside, wrapped up in a green paper bag. A police spokesmen said all three items were in excellent condition but he did not know where the two remaining statues might be.
The lion statue, which was made by Gabriel Orlandini in 1615, was wrenched from its marble pedestal in St Mark's Basilica, possibly during mass last Sunday.
The police spokesman said widespread media coverage of the robbery might have made it impossible for the thieves to sell the statue without drawing attention to themselves.
